t: You're on Hampstead Heath, an ancient heath of about 320 hectares. It sits on a sandy ridge running from Hampstead to Highgate, one of the highest points in London. It's rambling and hilly, with ponds, woodland, a lido and playgrounds, and it adjoins Kenwood House. At the south-east end is Parliament Hill, where the view over London is protected by law. The poet Adrian Mitchell, a leading voice of the anti-nuclear movement in Britain, was born here. Several others died here, including the artist Beatrice Whistler and the suffragette and philanthropist Lucy, Lady Houston.
